patch_description:
This implementation replaces the expensive full-region BFS validation and simulated annealing loop with a topology-aware randomized erosion method.

The key observation is that every accepted state preserves connectivity. Therefore, when removing one cell from a color, it is sufficient to test whether that cell's same-colored neighbors remain connected to each other; a full scan of the entire ward is unnecessary. Likewise, zero cells are only introduced from the exterior-connected zero component, so zero connectivity is maintained inductively.

The algorithm performs many randomized restarts. Within each restart it repeatedly:
- tries to convert frontier cells into exterior-connected color `0`,
- preserves every required adjacency and forbids every non-required adjacency,
- checks only local articulation behavior for the color losing a cell,
- occasionally performs connectivity-safe nonzero recoloring moves to reshape wards and unlock future erosion opportunities.

This uses local edge-count maintenance and local connectivity checks instead of global connectivity BFS after every move.
